To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) cloud computing is not a one-size-fits-all solution; (2) cloud computing is best used when the workload is highly variable, and (3) the cost of a cloud service is not directly proportional to its performance.

the cost of cloud computing for transaction processing is significantly lower than the cost of on-premise computing for transaction processing, but that the cost varies significantly depending on the vendor, the workload, and the amount of storage.
the performance of a transactional workload in the cloud depends on the architecture of the database management system (DBMS) and that there is no one size fits all architecture.

the question: How can we best exploit the cloud for transaction processing applications?
the question: How can we build a cloud service that is as good as a traditional database system in terms of throughput and cost?
